messages:
Samir: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change we saw a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate on canary (p50 latency up ~12%, token cost +9%). Profiler dump below, looks correlated with a change in batch shape + KV key churn.

Samir: profiler snippet:```
hot_prefix_hitrate: 0.28 -> 0.12
avg_batch_seq: 64 -> 42
kv_cache_entries: 4.2M -> 4.0M
mem_frag_ratio_gpu: 0.14 -> 0.27
kernel_path: fused_attn_v2 -> fused_attn_v3
```

Nisha: ugh. did the selector change alter input normalization or key hashing? small key fingerprint mismatch can drop effective hit-rate instantly. which commit?

Samir: selector change is rwd/runtime#4121 — main diff is fallthrough to v3 for seq<128 and new shape bucketing. I don't think we touched hashing but kernel v3 pads/trims prefixes differently.

Lee: that padding could change canonicalization. we should diff cache keys for identical requests pre/post. small script:```bash
# sample keys from logs
jq -r '.req_id + "\t" + .cache_key' /var/log/runtime/kv_keys.log | grep session123 | sort | uniq -c | head
```

Maria: also seeing higher GPU allocator fragmentation — pulse shows more small allocations after v3 (probably KV slab splits). fragmentation + slightly smaller effective cache capacity => eviction churn.

perf-bot: ALERT: canary-rg-7 hitrate drop > 10% sustained for 6m. Rolling pause on auto-rollout triggered.

Nisha: plan proposal: 1) collect N minutes of request pairs (pre/post) and diff normalized key fingerprints; 2) run offline replay with v3 but old key-normalizer to see if hit-rate stays low; 3) if keys changed, revert padding behavior or normalize before hashing; 4) as mitigation tune TTL buckets to reduce churn (longer hot-bucket TTL) and reduce aggressive soft-evict.

Samir: started capture: /tmp/canary_key_dump.pre and .post. uploading a 10k sample now.

Maria: experiment idea — try two quick config toggles on canary: (A) increase gpu_kv_soft_limit from 0.75 -> 0.85, (B) switch ttl_buckets: [8s, 32s, 128s, 512s] -> [16s, 64s, 256s, 1024s] to see hit-rate sensitivity. small rollout to 5% traffic.

Lee: FYI here's a small reg check to compute canonical key fingerprint ignoring padding:```python
def canonical_key(req):
    p = req['prompt']
    # strip trailing whitespace/newline padding used by v3
    p = p.rstrip('\n \t')
    h = hashlib.sha1(p.encode()).hexdigest()
    return h
```

Nisha: good. if that recovers keys -> we fix normalizer in runtime (hotfix) and keep v3. if not, look deeper at batch-induced KV index collisions.

Samir: ran offline replay with old normalizer + v3 kernel: hit-rate stable (0.31) — so padding is the culprit. keys diverge because v3 pads to 8-byte boundaries for packed-emb.

Maria: ok that explains fragmentation too. padding increases unique key entropy for small prompts. we can either canonicalize before hashing or make pad deterministic to not affect cache key. preference = canonicalize pre-hash.

Lee: implement quick fix: strip pad bytes when building cache key (small change). also add unit test to ensure identical keys across kernels.

Samir: PR up: rwd/runtime#4129 — key-canonicalizer: strip kernel padding + add regression test with padding permutations. will land to canary branch then re-run canary.

perf-bot: NOTE: deploy to canary started (5% traffic) by Samir.

Nisha: after landing, also run short mem-profiling pass to confirm fragmentation falls back below 0.18 and kv entries stabilize.

Maria: will monitor allocator histograms and eviction counter (evict/sec). if evict/sec doesn't drop within 10m revert.

Samir: initial canary numbers after fix (2m in): hot_prefix_hitrate: 0.13 -> 0.30, mem_frag_ratio_gpu: 0.26 -> 0.16, avg_batch_seq stable. p50 trending down.

Lee: nice. next follow-ups: - add canary regression that replays varied prompt padding - add metric for "keys_normalized" fraction - document kernel padding interactions in perf-runbook.

Nisha: also note long-term: consider moving key hashing post-kernel-compile invariant step or include a kernel version tag in cache-key to avoid cross-kernel collisions.

Maria: put a note in the rollout ticket about TTL tweak fallback option if we see transient blips during global rollout.

Samir: thanks team — landing to prod tomorrow A/B with 20% ramp if stable. :thumbsup:
